title: Finding files and matching text: retrieval check
markdown:
## Recall before you check

This retrieval pass revisits finding files and matching text without re-teaching it. Before you open the check, say in your own words how `find` selects files by name, type and modification time, how `grep` searches recursively and reports file names, and why filenames with spaces need `-print0` with `xargs -0` or `-exec ... {} +`. Recall the difference between a fixed-string search and a regular expression, and what `grep` exit status 1 means.

## What to bring back

- `find DIR -type f -name '*.log'` matches names against a quoted pattern; unquoted patterns expand in the shell first.
- `find DIR -mtime -1` selects files modified in the last day; `-newer FILE` compares against another file.
- `grep -rn PATTERN DIR` searches recursively with line numbers; `-l` lists only matching file names; `-F` treats the pattern as a fixed string.
- `find ... -print0 | xargs -0 CMD` keeps filenames with spaces intact; `-exec CMD {} +` runs the command with many files at once.
- `grep` exits 1 when nothing matched and 2 on an error such as an unreadable file.

The questions below use different examples from your lesson. Answer from memory first, then read the feedback.

key_takeaways: Quote find patterns so the shell does not expand them first.
Use -print0 with xargs -0 or -exec {} + for filenames with spaces.
grep status 1 means no match; 2 means an error.

questions.prompt: Which command lists only regular files ending in .log under `logs`, including subdirectories?
questions.explanation: -type f restricts to regular files; the quoted pattern is matched by find, not the shell.
questions.learning_objective: Select files by type and quoted name pattern

questions.prompt: You need the names of files under `src` that contain the text `TODO`, without the matching lines. Which option?
questions.explanation: -l prints only file names with at least one match; -r recurses.
questions.learning_objective: List matching files rather than lines

choices: Filenames are separated by NUL so spaces and newlines in names stay intact
It limits results to one file
questions.correct_answer: Filenames are separated by NUL so spaces and newlines in names stay intact
questions.explanation: NUL cannot appear in a filename, so it is the only safe separator.
questions.learning_objective: Pass awkward filenames safely to another command

questions.prompt: Which grep option searches for the literal text `a.b` rather than a pattern where `.` matches any character?
questions.explanation: -F treats the pattern as a fixed string.
questions.learning_objective: Choose fixed-string search when the text contains regex characters

choices: Regular files modified within the last day
questions.correct_answer: Regular files modified within the last day
questions.explanation: -mtime -1 selects modification times less than one day ago.
